content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti sauce with meat is a ready‑to‑use culinary product that combines a tomato base, minced beef or pork, spices and aromatic herbs. It is designed for quick preparation of classic spaghetti Bolognese and offers a rich, slightly sweet flavor with a hint of warmth.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato base is usually made from ripe tomatoes cooked down for several hours to deepen the flavor.
Traditional Italian Bolognese includes beef, pork and sometimes pancetta.
Carrots and celery are often added, enhancing aroma and nutritional value.
The sauce can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 5 days after opening or frozen for up to 3 months.
Some versions contain a splash of red wine, which adds depth to the taste.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat component provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and tomatoes supply vitamins B6 and B12, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The sauce contains iron, zinc and potassium, which contribute to normal blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Compared with many commercial sauces, this product typically contains only a small amount of added sugar.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made sauce can be fairly salty; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Some variants may contain wheat flour as a thickener; check the label if you have gluten intolerance.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain products use preservatives that may cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of the meat and oil, the sauce has a moderate to high calorie count; consider it within your overall diet.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Heat the sauce in a saucepan, add cooked spaghetti and stir. You can finish with grated Parmesan, fresh basil or a drizzle of olive oil. The sauce also works well in casseroles, lasagna and as a base for meat stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep it in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in a sealed bag for up to 3 months.
